system.title: System & maintenance
system.description: Status of the service, Usenet and capture with the key runtime facts, updates, and logs and retention.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.description: Back up the complete server configuration or restore an existing backup in a controlled flow.

general.title: Queue & retries
general.description: How many downloads run at once, with how many chunks and connections per host, how often they are retried — plus automatic removal and checksums.

network.title: Network & certificates
network.description: Proxy profiles and the global fallback, your own certificate authority, and the reconnect script.

media.title: Media, galleries & streams
media.description: Paths and limits for yt-dlp, gallery-dl and streamlink — the external helpers that turn links into downloads.

postprocess.title: Post-processing & delivery
postprocess.description: What happens to a finished package: repair, unpack, cleanup, run a script and optionally upload to an rclone remote.

interface.title: Interface
interface.description: Language, theme and notifications for this browser, plus, for every browser, how sizes, the tab title, cover images and the NZB hand-over are shown.

bandwidth.title: Bandwidth & budgets
bandwidth.description: Time-controlled profiles, limits per protocol, host, account or category, and daily or monthly traffic budgets.

notifications.title: Notifications & webhooks
notifications.description: Signed webhooks, e-mail and Apprise-compatible services, filtered by event, category and severity, with a delivery history.

services.title: Services
services.description: Switch off what this installation should not do. A switched-off service refuses new links and stops the ones it already had.

accounts.title: Provider accounts
accounts.description: Logins for hosters, debrid services and other providers. Every account uses its own isolated client identity — cookie jar, proxy, TLS — and no secret or cookie is ever returned by the API. Plus the sign-ins for protected sites.

security.title: Security
security.description: Second factor and passkeys for the login, the sessions signed in right now, and the reverse proxy this service may believe.

hotfolders.title: Hotfolders
hotfolders.description: Folders the service watches for NZB, torrent and container files, the category each one feeds, and how often all of them are checked.

unattended.title: Unattended operation
unattended.description: Quiet hours, what happens once the queue is empty, and pausing on battery or a metered connection.

captcha.title: Captcha & solver
captcha.description: Whether a captcha goes to a solver service or is asked of you in your browser, and how long an unanswered one waits.

torrent.title: BitTorrent
torrent.description: Listen port, sharing and seeding limits, the network interface and kill switch, blocklist and proxy for the built-in engine.

transfers.title: FTP, SFTP, WebDAV & S3
transfers.description: Stored logins for FTP, FTPS and SFTP servers, the SSH host keys you confirmed, the limits for remote transfers, and the profiles for S3-compatible object storage.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: Where yt-dlp, ffmpeg, gallery-dl, streamlink and the archivers are found, which version each one is, and the managed versions the service can install itself.

about.title: About rDownloader
about.description: Which version is running, where it comes from, who made it, and under which licenses the parts it ships are.

linkgrabber.title: LinkGrabber
linkgrabber.description: Which links the LinkGrabber drops before they reach it, how it opens DLC containers and whether it groups copies of one file as mirrors.

clients.title: Clients & API
clients.description: Pair the desktop client and the browser extension with this server, and issue API tokens for REST, the CLI, SABnzbd- and qBittorrent-compatible clients and the MCP server.

active_files.label: Simultaneous downloads
active_files.description: How many downloads run at once; also set in the status bar, and applied without a restart.

chunks.label: Chunks per file
chunks.description: Only when the server supports HTTP range requests

connections_per_host.label: Connections per host
connections_per_host.description: Applies to all downloads of the same host together; 0 lifts the limit

nntp_connections.label: NNTP connections per file
nntp_connections.description: 0 = as many as the servers allow; a lower number caps one file
nntp_connections.follows_servers: Every file uses every connection of each enabled server, currently {largest} on the largest.
nntp_connections.capped: The largest enabled server allows {largest} connections; one file gets at most {cap} per server. 0 uses them all.
nntp_connections.not_binding: Not binding: no enabled server allows more than {largest} connections.

retries.label: Retries per file
retries.description: Attempts after transient errors before a download counts as failed (0–100). Waiting out a hoster’s limit or IP block does not count.

import_history.label: Keep import history
import_history.description: Keep imported NZB entries and stored .torrent files after the download finishes. When disabled, they are removed automatically on completion — duplicate detection for re-imported NZBs is then unavailable.
import_history.title: Import history

auto_remove.label: Remove finished packages
auto_remove.description: A machine that downloads unattended fills its queue with finished packages. This clears them out after they have been finished for a while.
auto_remove.delay_description: Hours a finished package stays in the queue (1–720).
auto_remove.keep_failed_description: A package holding a file that did not finish is left alone.

mirrors.label: Recognise mirrors
mirrors.description: When a package holds several links to the same file, download one of them and keep the rest as fallbacks. If the one that runs gives up, another takes over.

sha256.label: Compute SHA-256
sha256.description: Compute a SHA-256 for every finished file whose source states no checksum; it is stored with the download.

admin_login.label: Disable admin login
admin_login.description: Whoever opens the interface on this computer may control everything without signing in. Every other machine — on the LAN, through a port mapping, a container or a reverse proxy — still has to sign in with the password. Takes effect immediately after saving.
admin_login.title: Sign-in on this computer

proxy.title: Connection routes (proxy profiles)
proxy.description: Profiles can be assigned globally, per account or per download. Passwords are stored encrypted.
proxy.name_description: Shown wherever the profile can be assigned.
proxy.kind_description: SOCKS5 resolves DNS names on the proxy (socks5h).
proxy.endpoint_description: Scheme, host and port, e.g. socks5h://127.0.0.1:1080.
proxy.username_description: Only needed for proxies that require authentication.
proxy.password_description: Stored encrypted and never returned by the API.
proxy.password_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored password
proxy.password_copy: The copy of {name} has no password: enter it again, the service takes the username only together with it.

delete.title: Delete proxy profile
delete.description: The proxy profile “{name}” and its encrypted password will be deleted permanently. While an account, a Usenet server, an unfinished download, the global connection route or the torrent peer proxy uses it, the service refuses.
delete.in_use_here: It is chosen here as the global connection route or the torrent peer proxy — choose another one first and save.

global_proxy.title: Global connection route
global_proxy.description: Used only when neither the download nor its account sets a proxy profile.
global_proxy.label: Connection route

custom_ca.label: Custom CA (PEM)
custom_ca.description: Additional trusted certificate authority; empty uses only the platform trust store.

postprocess.title: Post-processing pipeline
postprocess.description: Packages and categories can override the level and script.

default_level.label: Default level
default_level.description: Applies to packages and categories without their own level.

pause.label: Pause downloads during post-processing
pause.description: Holds new downloads while a package is being repaired or unpacked.

cleanup_extensions.label: Cleanup extensions
cleanup_extensions.description: Files with these extensions (without dot) are deleted from the package folder after unpacking.

ignore_samples.label: Ignore samples
ignore_samples.description: Deletes sample files after unpacking and skips sample archives.

recursive_unpack.label: Recursive unpacking
recursive_unpack.description: Also extract archives found inside extracted archives (up to 3 levels deep). Inner archives are removed after extraction.

sfv_verify.label: SFV verification
sfv_verify.description: Check the CRC32 checksums of any .sfv index in the package before unpacking. A mismatching or missing file fails the package.

safe_postproc.label: Post-process only verified packages
safe_postproc.description: After a failed PAR2, SFV or RAR check nothing is unpacked, tidied or handed to plugin steps. On by default, as in SABnzbd. Off: a broken recovery set beside intact archives no longer locks the package.

delete_par2.label: Delete PAR2 files after unpacking
delete_par2.description: Removes the recovery set once repair and extraction have both succeeded. Off by default: PAR2 data is the only thing that can rescue a damaged package, and a retry after a failed unpack still needs it.

enable_all_par.label: Download all PAR2 volumes
enable_all_par.description: Fetches every recovery volume of an NZB straight away. Off: only the main index comes down with the payload, the vol volumes wait, and a repair re-queues exactly as many of them as the gap needs.

plugin_steps.label: Plugin steps
plugin_steps.description: Extra steps contributed by installed plugins. They run after cleanup and before a user script, in the order you switch them on; a category can override this list.

sample_max.label: Sample size limit
sample_max.description: Files named like samples are only treated as samples up to this size.

scripts_directory.label: Scripts directory
scripts_directory.description: Absolute path; empty = scripts next to the database. Only file names from this folder can be selected.

script_timeout.label: Script timeout
script_timeout.description: Seconds after which a post-processing script is killed (10–86400).

passwords_file.label: Password list
passwords_file.description: One password per line; empty = passwords.txt next to the database. Tried after the package password and "no password".

rar_executable.label: External RAR tool
rar_executable.description: Optional absolute path to unrar or 7z; invoked without a shell.

upload.label: Upload to rclone remote
upload.description: Copies or moves the finished package folder to an rclone remote as the last step. Remotes come from your rclone.conf.

upload_remote.label: Upload target
upload_remote.description: rclone target in remote:path form; each package gets its own folder below it.

upload_mode.label: Upload mode
upload_mode.description: Move deletes the local files after a successful upload.

rclone_executable.label: rclone executable
rclone_executable.description: Optional absolute path to rclone; empty = vendor folders and PATH.

enrichment.label: Ask enricher plugins about links
enrichment.description: Off by default. An enricher looks a link up at a service outside this machine — SponsorBlock, for one — so nothing is asked until you say so. Only links a plugin claims are sent, and what comes back is shown beside the core details, never instead of them.

unpack_to_subfolder.label: Unpack into subfolders
unpack_to_subfolder.description: Unpack each archive into a folder of its own inside the package folder, named after the archive (Film.part1.rar → Film/). The archives themselves are not moved.

malware_scan.label: Scan packages for malware (ClamAV)
malware_scan.description: Every finished package goes to your clamd after unpacking, before plugin steps, the script or the upload see it. A finding stops the package; if clamd cannot be reached, it carries on with a warning. Nothing leaves this machine except to this address.
malware_scan.address_description: host:port for TCP or unix:/path for the local socket; empty = 127.0.0.1:3310.
malware_scan.max_description: Larger files are not scanned and are counted on the step. StreamMaxLength in clamd.conf has to be at least this large.
malware_scan.timeout_description: How long the connection, one chunk or clamd’s verdict may take (5–3600 s).

fail_hopeless_jobs.label: Abort hopeless Usenet downloads
fail_hopeless_jobs.description: When more PAR2 blocks are missing than the set's recovery volumes can replace, the rest is not downloaded and the package fails. What has been downloaded stays. Saves volume on block accounts. Off: every file is downloaded to the end, as before.

direct_unpack.label: Unpack while downloading
direct_unpack.description: Multi-part RAR archives from Usenet are unpacked part by part as each part arrives complete, instead of after the download. If a repair is needed or a part is missing something, the attempt is dropped and the archive is unpacked afterwards as usual. Needs unrar and room for the unpacked files beside the running download.

unwrap_package_folder.label: Dissolve a folder named like the package
unwrap_package_folder.description: When the package folder holds nothing but one folder named like the package after post-processing (Release/Release/…), its content moves up one level and the empty folder is removed. With subfolders per archive, the same applies to each archive's folder. Nothing is ever overwritten. Works only when nothing else is left in the package folder — so let the source archive go, e.g. with the level "+Delete".

package_names.label: Tidy package names
package_names.description: Tidies a new package's name before its folder is created, with the same rules as the “Tidy file names” plugin, which renames the files inside the folder. Applies only to names rDownloader derives itself (from file names, NZB files, torrents); a name you give or rename stays as it is. Each category can override the switches.

strip_bracket_tags.label: Remove bracket tags
strip_bracket_tags.description: Tags in square, round or curly brackets such as [1080p] or (x264) are removed, brackets and all.

collapse_separators.label: Collapse separators
collapse_separators.description: Runs of dots, underscores, hyphens and spaces become one separator and are trimmed at both ends: Big..Buck_-_Bunny → Big.Buck.Bunny

regex.label: Regex rules
regex.description: Find and replace after the switches, in this order; every match is replaced, $1, $2 … insert groups. At most 10 rules. A name that would become empty stays as it was.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: Language, theme and browser notifications are stored in this browser only and take effect immediately.

byte_display.label: Data sizes
byte_display.description: Decides how sizes and speeds are shown everywhere in the interface.

byte_unit.label: Data size unit
byte_unit.description: Automatic picks the fitting magnitude for each value. A fixed unit shows every value in the same one, so a list can be compared column by column.

title_status.label: State in the browser tab
title_status.description: While something is running the tab shows the overall rate and the number of active transfers, and the application name alone otherwise. Off if a title that keeps changing is a distraction.

messages.reset_done: All runtime settings were reset to their defaults.
messages.number_empty: A number field is empty. Enter a value to save.

reset.title: Restore factory settings?
reset.description: All runtime settings will be reset to the built-in defaults. Storage roots, categories, rules, accounts, servers, tokens and downloads are kept.

media.title: Video & audio (yt-dlp)
media.description: Links from the media hosts are probed with yt-dlp and offered as video/audio variants in the LinkGrabber.

ffmpeg.label: ffmpeg executable
ffmpeg.description: Needed for MP3 conversion and for merging separate video/audio streams.

default_variant.label: Default variant
default_variant.description: Preselected for new media links; changeable per link in the LinkGrabber.

hosts.label: Media hosts
hosts.description: Hosts (without www.) handled by the media provider instead of the HTTP downloader.
hosts.add_defaults_hint: Merges the built-in host list into your entries. Nothing is removed – existing installations pick up newly added hosts this way.
hosts.defaults_complete: All default hosts are already present.

check_timeout.label: Probe timeout
check_timeout.description: Seconds one metadata probe may take before the link counts as offline (5–600).

status.unavailable: Tool status could not be loaded.
status.hint: MP3 output and merging separate video/audio streams require ffmpeg.

output_template.label: Output template
output_template.description: Arranges media downloads inside the package folder. Folders are separated by /. Empty keeps the plain file name. Each link can override this.

ui_port.label: Web interface port
ui_port.description: Port the web UI listens on (1024–65535); empty keeps the built-in default.
ui_port.restart_hint: Takes effect after a restart. --listen and RDOWNLOADER_LISTEN override this value.

collector.title: Blocklist
collector.description: Links whose host is on the blocklist are dropped before they reach the LinkGrabber.

excluded_domains.label: Excluded domains file
excluded_domains.description: Absolute path to the blocklist; empty = excluded_domains.txt next to the database.

format.title: File format
format.comments: Lines starting with # are comments and are ignored.
format.www: A leading www. is optional and matches either way.
format.subdomains: A host also blocks all of its subdomains.

dlc.title: DLC containers
dlc.description: A DLC holds its links encrypted and cannot be decrypted on this machine. Importing one asks an online service for the container key.

enabled.label: Allow DLC import
enabled.description: Off by default. While it is off, a dropped .dlc is refused instead of being sent anywhere.
enabled.warning: Every import sends the container's key to the service below. The links themselves stay here.

indexer_images.title: Cover images
indexer_images.description: An indexer sends a cover address alongside each hit, in the same search answer the subscription already makes. Showing it costs no extra request; loading the picture is done by the browser.

enabled.label: Show cover images
enabled.description: On by default. While it is off, the details of a hit stay visible and only the pictures are left unloaded, so the indexer is not told which hits are on screen.

nzb_hand_over.title: Hand to provider
nzb_hand_over.description: An NZB can be handed to an account whose provider takes NZB files (such as TorBox or Premiumize): from the LinkGrabber before it is queued, or from the Downloads, for instance when a package failed. The provider fetches the NZB from Usenet itself; the finished files come back into the LinkGrabber as links.

linkgrabber.label: Show the hand-over in the LinkGrabber
linkgrabber.description: On by default. The menu in each NZB row and the entry in the selection bar appear only while you have an account with a provider that takes NZB files (TorBox, Premiumize). An import already handed over keeps its badge.

downloads.label: Show the hand-over in the Downloads
downloads.description: On by default. The entry in the menu of a package that came from an NZB appears in any state of the package, failed included, but only while you have an account with a provider that takes NZB files (TorBox, Premiumize). A package already handed over keeps its badge.

notifications.label: Browser notifications
notifications.description: Shows a desktop notification when a download or post-processing job finishes. Stored in this browser only.
notifications.denied: The browser blocked notifications for this page. Allow them in the site permissions and switch the toggle on again.
notifications.unsupported: This browser does not support notifications.

vendor.title: Tool discovery
vendor.description: yt-dlp, ffmpeg, ffprobe, unrar, 7z, rclone, gallery-dl, streamlink and apprise are looked up in the explicit setting first, then in the vendor folders and finally in PATH.

directory.title: Vendor folder
directory.label: Vendor directory
directory.description: Absolute directory searched before PATH; empty = the built-in vendor folders next to the executable and in the data directory.

vendor.hint: Drop the binaries into a vendor folder next to the executable and they work without touching PATH.
vendor.ffprobe_warning: ffmpeg was found but ffprobe was not. Without ffprobe yt-dlp cannot merge separate video and audio streams or convert audio to MP3. Both binaries ship together – copy ffprobe next to ffmpeg.

compatibility.warning: At least one tool is too old or listed as broken. Only the capabilities named below are blocked; everything else keeps downloading.

gallery.title: Gallery downloads (gallery-dl)
gallery.description: Image galleries from the listed hosts are fetched with gallery-dl; each gallery becomes one queue entry with its own folder. Site logins live in your gallery-dl.conf.

executable.label: gallery-dl executable
executable.description: Optional absolute path; empty = vendor folders and PATH.

max_parallel.label: Concurrent galleries
max_parallel.description: Galleries downloading at the same time (1–8).

hosts.label: Gallery hosts
hosts.description: Links from these hosts are routed to gallery-dl (media hosts win when listed in both).
hosts.hint: gallery-dl supports many more sites; add any host it can handle.

streams.title: Stream recording (streamlink)
streams.description: Recordings are exempt from the global download slots; their own limit below applies.

executable.label: streamlink executable
executable.description: Optional absolute path; empty = vendor folders (incl. vendor/streamlink/bin) and PATH.

quality.label: Default quality
quality.description: Quality preset used when a channel has no selection of its own.

poll_interval.label: Channel poll interval
poll_interval.description: Seconds between liveness probes of enabled channels (60–3600).

max_parallel.label: Concurrent recordings
max_parallel.description: Recordings running at the same time (1–8).

torrent.title: Torrents (built-in engine)
torrent.description: Torrents and magnet links run in the embedded engine with DHT, trackers and PEX. Web seeds (BEP 19) are not supported.

sharing.label: Share data with other peers
sharing.description: Off by default: nothing is uploaded, not even while a torrent is still downloading.
sharing.leech_only_warning: Downloading without ever uploading is unfair to the swarm, and some private trackers ban clients that do it.

seeding.label: Seed finished torrents
seeding.description: Keep uploading after the download; the row completes when a limit below is reached.

seed_ratio.label: Seed ratio limit
seed_ratio.description: Stop seeding at uploaded/downloaded ratio; 0 disables the ratio stop.

seed_time.label: Seed time limit
seed_time.description: Stop seeding after this many minutes; empty = no time limit.

listen_port.label: Listen port
listen_port.description: Incoming peer connections; empty = a random port.

upload_limit.label: Upload limit
upload_limit.description: Global torrent upload limit; empty = unlimited.

torrent.restart_hint: Port and upload limit apply after the next service restart; the seeding limits apply immediately.

peer_addresses.label: Show full peer addresses
peer_addresses.description: Off by default: a peer address is personal data of a third party, and the network prefix is enough to judge a swarm. Addresses are never written to a log or an event either way.

bind_interface.label: Bind to network interface
bind_interface.description: All torrent sockets use this interface only. Combined with the kill switch this is what makes a VPN tunnel safe.

kill_switch.label: Stop when the interface disappears
kill_switch.description: Pauses every torrent within ten seconds of the bound interface going away, and resumes when it returns.

listen_mode.label: Peer transports
listen_mode.description: Which incoming peer connections the listener accepts.

peer_limit.label: Peers per torrent
peer_limit.description: Maximum peer connections per torrent; empty leaves it to the engine.

blocklist.label: IP blocklist URL
blocklist.description: An http or https URL the engine loads at startup. A blocklist that fails to load only affects torrents, never other downloads.

proxy.label: SOCKS5 proxy for peer connections
proxy.description: Applies to outgoing peer connections only. Tracker announces and metadata requests are not routed through it — this engine cannot proxy them separately.

upnp.label: Forward the listen port (UPnP)
upnp.description: Asks the router to map the listen port. A mapping that fails never blocks outgoing downloads. NAT-PMP and PCP are not supported.

announce_port.label: Announced port
announce_port.description: Port announced to trackers when the router maps the listen port to a different external one. Empty announces the listen port.

network_status.title: Network status
network_status.description: What the torrent engine is doing right now: the bound interface, the kill switch and the last session rebuild.
network_status.kill_switch_armed: Armed: pauses torrents within {seconds} s of the interface disappearing
network_status.engaged_title: The kill switch has paused the torrents
network_status.engaged_description: The interface {name} is gone. Once it returns, the torrents resume on their own.
network_status.rebuild_failed: The last session rebuild failed; the previous session keeps running.
network_status.proxy_failed: The peer proxy cannot be resolved; without it the session does not start.

auth_profiles.approval_description: These sessions were sent by the browser extension. They are only used once you approve them.
auth_profiles.certificate_description: Private key and certificate chain as one decrypted PEM bundle. Passphrase-protected keys are not supported.
auth_profiles.delete_description: The stored credentials are deleted with it. Jobs pinned to it fall back to automatic matching.
auth_profiles.description: Reuse a browser session or send HTTP credentials to one approved domain. Cookies, tokens and private keys are stored encrypted and never shown again.
auth_profiles.expires_description: Optional. An expired profile stays listed but is no longer used.
auth_profiles.scope_description: Host, optionally with a path prefix. The path decides which profile matches, it does not confine the credential.
auth_profiles.secret_cookies_description: Netscape cookies.txt content or a Cookie header.
auth_profiles.secret_keep: Leave empty to keep the stored value.
auth_profiles.title: Authentication profiles

storage.title: Storage capacity
storage.description: Applies to every transport. A destination below its threshold takes no new downloads until space is free again. A storage root’s own “Minimum free space” above overrides the global value for that root.

minimum_free.label: Minimum free space
minimum_free.description: Kept free on every storage root without an own threshold.

headroom.label: Headroom for unknown sizes
headroom.description: A transfer that states no size may start while this multiple of the threshold is free (1–64).

auto_resume.label: Resume automatically
auto_resume.description: Releases a blocked destination as soon as it has room again; off requires the manual resume action.

collision.label: On a name collision
collision.description: What happens when a finished file meets a name that is taken – for packages and categories without a policy of their own.

activity.title: Moves, links and reuse
activity.description: Verified moves between folders, duplicate links, and what each kind of transfer reuses of data already on disk.
activity.index_checked: Content index checked: {checked} entries, {missing} missing, {restored} found again, {backfilled} added.
activity.links_description: Found out by trying. This build creates no reflinks.
activity.reuse_description: Declared by each runner itself: resume, re-check, adopt, verify, and whether the collision policy applies to it.
activity.history_description: Newest first. A move between devices is verified by SHA-256 before the original is removed.

services.title: Transfer services
services.description: Every service is on until you switch it off here. What is off refuses matching links at intake and blocks anything of that kind already in the queue, with a reason.
services.hint: Switching a service back on releases its blocked rows; they return to the queue.

torrent.label: BitTorrent
torrent.description: Magnet links, .torrent files and the peer-to-peer engine.

media.label: Media downloads
media.description: Video and audio links resolved by yt-dlp.

remote.label: Remote file transfer
remote.description: FTP, FTPS, SFTP and WebDAV links.

off.title: Service switched off: {name}
off.description: Matching links are refused at intake, and queued rows of this kind wait blocked. The settings here apply once you switch the service back on.

managed_tools.title: Tool versions
managed_tools.description: rDownloader can download, verify and activate yt-dlp, gallery-dl, Streamlink, ffmpeg and ffprobe itself. Every version comes from a signed manifest and is confirmed by its checksum before it is activated.
managed_tools.enabled_description: Off unless you say otherwise: downloading executables is not something to start unasked. An explicitly configured path still takes precedence.
managed_tools.manifest_url_description: https address of the signed tool manifest. Empty = only the manifest shipped with this build, which works safely without a network.
managed_tools.disabled_description: Switch on "Manage tools automatically" above to download and activate versions. The programs already found stay exactly as they are.
managed_tools.manifest_built_in: The manifest built into this release
managed_tools.activated: {tool} now runs in the version you chose.
managed_tools.rolled_back: {tool} is back on its previous version.
managed_tools.refreshed: The manifest was verified and adopted.
managed_tools.hint: A running job keeps the version it started with: activating another one takes effect for the next job, and a version in use is never removed.
managed_tools.overrides_description: The verdict is still shown for the tools chosen here, but it is not enforced. Every block skipped this way is written to the log.

logs.title: Log retention
logs.description: How much of the structured log the service keeps. Older records are removed in the background; the queue never waits for it.
logs.days_description: Records older than this are removed whatever the count (1-365).

audit.title: Audit log and trace export
audit.description: How long the append-only audit log is kept, and whether finished spans are sent to an OpenTelemetry collector. The export is off until you switch it on.
audit.records_description: The oldest whole records go first (10000-2000000).
audit.days_description: Records older than this are removed whatever the count (30-3650).
audit.otlp_enabled_description: Off by default. A collector that is down or slow never delays a download or a request.
audit.otlp_endpoint_description: The OTLP/HTTP traces URL, for example http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces.
audit.otlp_timeout_description: How long one attempt may take before it is abandoned (1-60 seconds).

overview.title: Settings
overview.description: Every page, grouped by what it is about. Open one here or pick it from the sidebar.

credits.title: Who makes rDownloader
credits.author: Author
credits.thanks: rDownloader is built on the projects listed below – thanks to everyone who writes and maintains them.

licenses.title: What ships with it
licenses.own_text: Free software under {license}; the full text is LICENSE in the package.
licenses.tools_hint: The Linux and Windows packages ship them under vendor/, their license texts under vendor/licenses/.
licenses.dependencies_hint: Everything a shipped package contains: the crates the service, the capture agent and the plugins link on Linux, Windows and macOS, and the packages of the interface. Generated at build time from Cargo.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml, never kept by hand.

nntp_parallel_files.label: Usenet files at once
nntp_parallel_files.description: 0 = automatic: as many as keep every connection busy (2 to 8). Together they take a single parallel-files slot.

upload_limit.label: Upload limit
upload_limit.description: Applies to every upload: torrent seeding, object storage, rclone and upload destinations. Empty means unlimited

auto_retry.label: Retry failed downloads automatically
auto_retry.description: A download that failed on a limit, an IP block, an unreachable server or a file reported offline goes back into the queue after a while. A deleted link, a refused account or a wrong checksum does not.
auto_retry.interval_description: Hours between the failure and the next attempt (1–24).
auto_retry.rounds_description: How often a download goes back into the queue at most; 0 means no limit (0–100).

history.title: Download history retention
history.description: How long finished and failed packages stay in the history after they left the list.
history.days_description: Entries older than this are removed whatever the count (1-3650).

limits.title: Download and upload limits
limits.description: Apply at all times, whatever the schedule. An active profile overlays them: the stricter of the two limits applies.

nntp_limits.title: NNTP connections and files
nntp_limits.description: The connections set per provider above are the ceiling: one file uses at most as many connections as each provider allows, and the cap here can hold it below that. Usenet files running at once share the providers’ connections.

tool_paths.title: Custom paths
tool_paths.description: A path here comes before the search in the vendor folders and PATH; an empty field leaves it to that search. Which file was found is shown by the tool discovery below.

display.title: Display
display.description: Saved with the settings in the service and applies in every browser that opens it.
